definition: Convergent means coming together toward the same point or answer from different starting places.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word convergent. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know convergent should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The rival startups drew up convergent designs for the delivery drone, each arriving at the same four-rotor frame before either had seen the other's plans.
Similar is weaker than convergent: similar findings merely resemble one another, while convergent findings are actively closing on the same answer from different directions.
Merged goes further than convergent — convergent paths are still distinct as they close in, but merged ones have already collapsed into a single line.
Intersecting paths simply cross once, at whatever angle, and carry on their separate ways. Convergent paths are aimed at the same point — the whole story is the closing distance.
Aligned means already in agreement, sitting on the same line. Convergent stresses the approach: different starting places, with the gap still closing.

Convergent means coming together toward the same point or answer from different starting places.
Dolphins are mammals and ichthyosaurs were reptiles, yet the fossil casts show the same torpedo body and the same tail-driven stroke.
Biologists call it convergent evolution: two distant lineages arriving at one design, because the sea poses every fast swimmer the same problem.
Convergent describes lines, paths, or conclusions that start far apart and close toward the same point.
The separate starting places are half the meaning — things that were never apart have nothing to close — and the drawing-together is the other half.
Convergent is the analyst's adjective — evidence, evolution, opinions, lines.
Use it when separate starting points are closing on one answer, and let the unit-mates handle the aftermath: a confluence is the meeting itself, and things that coalesce have already fused.
Convergent is the approach, still in motion.
